title: Sean Connery, 007 and the Rolex Submariner

slides.title: Bond's creator gave him a Rolex. *He didn't own one.*
slides.body: How a dive watch became 007's signature, and why Ian Fleming nearly took it away.

image.credit: Sean Connery, Switzerland 1964 · Comet Photo AG / ETH-Bibliothek Zürich · CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.title: Bond's first *Rolex*
slides.body: In the novel *Live and Let Die*, Bond checks the Rolex on his wrist while swimming underwater. Then, for the next eight books, **Bond doesn't wear one.**

slides.title: Fleming *says no*
slides.body: A reader writes that Bond should wear a Rolex. Fleming replies that it's too heavy for a fight, and that Bond prefers **cheap, expendable watches** he can use as a knuckle-duster.

slides.title: Then comes *Dr. No*
slides.body: On screen, Sean Connery's Bond wears a **Rolex Submariner ref. 6538**, the “Big Crown” dive watch. Around the same time, Fleming buys his own Rolex, an Explorer.

image.credit: Submariner ref. 6538, late 1950s · Photo: EMore98 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Whose watch *was it?*
slides.body: The popular story says producer Cubby Broccoli took the Rolex off his own wrist and handed it to Connery. **Nobody has ever proven it**, and other versions of the story exist.

slides.title: The strap that *wasn't* NATO
slides.body: In *Goldfinger*, Bond wears it on a striped nylon strap. Fans call it a NATO strap, but **the real NATO strap was only created in 1973.**

slides.title: A mystery on *his wrist*
slides.body: Connery wears a 6538 in *Dr. No*, *From Russia with Love*, *Goldfinger* and *Thunderball*. **Where the screen-worn watch ended up is still unknown.**

slides.title: Bond *switches brands*
slides.body: A Rolex last appears on Bond's wrist in 1989. In *GoldenEye*, Pierce Brosnan wears an **Omega Seamaster**, and Omega has stayed on 007's wrist ever since.

slides.title: Shaken, not stirred. *Waterproof to 200 m.*
slides.next: Royal Oak: the steel watch that shocked the luxury world

caption:
Ian Fleming gave James Bond a Rolex in 1954. Four years later, he said Bond preferred cheap watches. 🍸⌚

Then Dr. No arrived in 1962, and Sean Connery's Submariner 6538 turned a tool watch into a legend. How it got onto his wrist is still disputed, and where it went is still unknown.

Which Bond watch is your favorite? 👇

Sources: WatchTime (2009); NATO; New Atlas; Bob's Watches; Wikipedia.
